question:
Refer to the exhibit. What does this output indicate about port channel 1?
switch# show interface po1
port-channel 1 is trunking
  admin port mode is F, trunk mode is on
  port mode is TF
options: Port channel 1 is configured as an ISL trunk between two MDS switches.
Port channel 1 is configured to connect to an NPV switch.
Port channel 1 is operating in NPIV mode.
Port channel 1 has negotiated E port mode.
theory: An FC port channel report of 'admin port mode is F, port mode is TF' shows the local switch's ports configured as F ports (trunk mode on) that have negotiated a Trunking F port (TF) state with the far end - TF ports are what a core/NPIV switch uses toward an NPV edge switch's NP uplinks, since an NPV edge relaying multiple VSANs still logs in through F/NP port pairs rather than the E/TE ports used between two full fabric switches. This output therefore indicates the port channel connects to an NPV switch, not another full fabric switch (which would show E/TE) nor an NPIV mode marker on the local port itself. (CCNP/CCIE DCCOR Official Cert Guide, Chapter 8 - NPIV and NPV)
